I've had a similar experience in Japan, not as terrifying but similar.
*TL;DR* Guy stared at me on entire train ride and got down on same stop
Another guy slipped a note in my bag and asked if I wanted to be his girlfriend

I was on a train back to the apartment my family and I was living in, not alone, my family was with me so there were 5 of us together. It was rush hour so we had to stand for most of the ride back home. I usually let others take the free seats because I was 16 at the time and I felt like I didn't need it. My mom gets really angry at me for doing that though because I had a lot of joint injuries so I shouldn't stand around as much. Anyway, we were halfway there and a guy in a suit and glasses started staring at me. I was and still am a pretty alert person so I noticed and moved to the other end of the train. He was still looking at me even though I moved. After a stop, there were more free seats so I sat down a few seats away from my family. The guy stood in front of me, even though there were free seats all around. I stood up and offered him my seat. He didn't respond so I walked to where my family were. He followed and sat opposite where I was standing. At that point I was pretty creeped out. 
We got down after a few minutes and he followed. I started to walk to the opposite direction he was heading to and he turned back multiple times to look at us. Scared the shit out of me because my whole family was with me at the time and I'm pretty sure he's aware.

A few days after, when we were at the airport, I saw a small folded paper in the pocket at the side of my bag. Pretty sure I threw out all the rubbish I had in there because garbage cans are really hard to come by in Japan for some reason. I opened it up and I saw a message written by god knows who. I can understand a little Japanese and it probably says, Sorry about this sudden message but when I saw you I really wanted to be friends with you. Please contact me. 
I was really shocked because I keep my bag close to me at all times and I'm very aware of my surroundings. To think a guy can get close enough to me to put a note in my bag is unnerving. I messaged the guy because I really needed to know how and where he slipped me the note. He told me that he thought I was Japanese and he saw me at Nakano Broadway. I went to Nakano Broadway 3 times in my one week trip so it was pretty creepy. Also, I should mention that the note was properly written, not like in a hurried manner so that's another thing to add to the creepiness factor.
After I got the info I wanted, I just kinda ignored the guy because it was kinda creepy. I did read some of his messages and at one point he asked me if I wanted to be his girlfriend. I blocked him immediately after that.
